# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by `go run ./tools/configref` from pkg/config. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every key Odin reads from its YAML configuration file. Keys not listed here are ignored.
Durations are written like `30s`, `5m` or `1h30m`. Any value can come from the environment as
`${NAME}` (required) or `${NAME:-default}`. Services can also live in a `services.yaml` next to
the main file. For a guided introduction see [Concepts](../concepts.md).

## `server`

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `server.port` | integer | Port to listen on (default 8080; GATEWAY_PORT overrides it). |
| `server.timeout` | duration | Not used by the request path; per-service timeouts are services[].timeout. |
| `server.readTimeout` | duration | Maximum time to read a whole request, including the body (default 30s). |
| `server.writeTimeout` | duration | Maximum time to write a response (default 30s). Long streams need a larger value. |
| `server.gracefulTimeout` | duration | How long shutdown waits for in-flight requests (default 15s). |
| `server.readHeaderTimeout` | duration | ReadHeaderTimeout bounds reading request headers (default 10s); IdleTimeout bounds idle keep-alive connections (default 120s). |
| `server.idleTimeout` | duration | How long idle keep-alive connections are kept (default 120s). |
| `server.compression` | boolean | Gzip responses for clients that accept it. |
| `server.maxBodySize` | string | MaxBodySize limits request bodies on proxied routes, e.g. "10M" (default) or "512K". |
| `server.trustedProxies` | list of string | TrustedProxies lists the proxy addresses or CIDRs whose X-Forwarded-For header is believed. With none, the client IP is the connection's address, so clients cannot spoof it to dodge rate limits or login throttling. |
| `server.debugEndpoints` | boolean | DebugEndpoints exposes /debug/routes and friends. Off by default: they list every route. |

## `logging`

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `logging.level` | string | debug, info (default), warn or error. |
| `logging.json` | boolean | Write logs as JSON instead of text. |

## `auth`

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auth.jwtSecret` | string | HMAC secret for verifying JWTs. ODIN_JWT_SECRET or an auth_secrets.yaml file take precedence. |
| `auth.accessTokenTTL` | duration | Not used by the gateway (it verifies tokens, it does not issue them). |
| `auth.refreshTokenTTL` | duration | Not used by the gateway. |
| `auth.ignorePathRegexes` | list of string | Request paths (regular expressions) that skip JWT checks, e.g. ^/health$. |
| `auth.issuer` | string | Issuer, when set, must match the token's iss claim. |
| `auth.audience` | string | Audience, when set, must be in the token's aud claim. |
| `auth.leeway` | duration | Leeway tolerates clock skew when checking exp, nbf and iat. |

## `rateLimit`

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rateLimit.enabled` | boolean | Apply limit per duration to every HTTP service, per client (the JWT subject, or the client IP). |
| `rateLimit.limit` | integer | Requests allowed per duration and client. 0 means no limit. |
| `rateLimit.duration` | duration | Length of the rate-limit window (default 1m). |
| `rateLimit.strategy` | string | local (default) or redis |
| `rateLimit.redisUrl` | string | Redis for strategy: redis, e.g. redis://redis:6379/0. |
| `rateLimit.algorithm` | string | Algorithm is fixed_window (default), sliding_window or token_bucket. |
| `rateLimit.failClosed` | boolean | FailClosed rejects requests when Redis is unreachable instead of allowing them. |

## `cache`

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cache.enabled` | boolean | Cache GET responses of HTTP services (only safe ones: no credentials, no cookies, no private or no-store). |
| `cache.ttl` | duration | How long entries live, unless the upstream's max-age is shorter. |
| `cache.redisUrl` | string | Redis for strategy: redis. |
| `cache.strategy` | string | local (default, in memory) or redis (shared by all instances). |
| `cache.maxSizeInMB` | integer | Not enforced yet. |

## `monitoring`

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `monitoring.enabled` | boolean | Serve Prometheus metrics. |
| `monitoring.path` | string | Metrics path (default /metrics). |
| `monitoring.webhookUrl` | string | Optional webhook for health alerts |

## `admin`

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `admin.enabled` | boolean | Serve the admin interface under /admin. Off by default; when off, no admin route exists. |
| `admin.username` | string | Admin login name (default admin; ODIN_ADMIN_USERNAME overrides it). |
| `admin.password` | string | Admin password in plain text. Prefer passwordHash or ODIN_ADMIN_PASSWORD; without any, a random password is logged at startup. |
| `admin.passwordHash` | string | PasswordHash is a bcrypt hash of the admin password; when set, Password is ignored. |
| `admin.allowedOrigins` | list of string | AllowedOrigins lists further origins (scheme://host[:port]) the admin accepts form posts and API writes from, for proxies that change the Host header (for example GitHub Codespaces port forwarding). By default only the admin's own origin is accepted. ODIN_ADMIN_ALLOWED_ORIGINS adds a comma-separated list. |

## `plugins`

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plugins.enabled` | boolean | Run Go plugins (built with -buildmode=plugin) on requests. |
| `plugins.directory` | string | Directory plugins are uploaded to and loaded from (default /var/odin/plugins). |
| `plugins.plugins` | list of objects | Plugins to load at startup. |
| `plugins.plugins[].name` | string | Unique plugin name. |
| `plugins.plugins[].path` | string | Path to the .so file. |
| `plugins.plugins[].enabled` | boolean | Load this plugin. |
| `plugins.plugins[].config` | map of string to any | Settings passed to the plugin's Initialize. |
| `plugins.plugins[].hooks` | list of string | pre-request, post-request, pre-response, post-response |

## `tracing`

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tracing.enabled` | boolean | Export OpenTelemetry traces over OTLP/HTTP and propagate trace context to upstreams. |
| `tracing.serviceName` | string | service.name of the spans (default odin-gateway). |
| `tracing.serviceVersion` | string | service.version of the spans (default 1.0.0). |
| `tracing.environment` | string | deployment.environment of the spans (default development). |
| `tracing.endpoint` | string | OTLP/HTTP endpoint, as a URL or host:port (default http://localhost:4318/v1/traces). |
| `tracing.sampleRate` | number | Fraction of traces sampled, 0 to 1 (default 1). |
| `tracing.insecure` | boolean | Use plain HTTP to a host:port endpoint. |

## `services`

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `services[].name` | string | Unique service name; used in metrics, logs and rate-limit keys. |
| `services[].basePath` | string | Path prefix routed to this service, e.g. /api/users (matches /api/users and /api/users/...). |
| `services[].targets` | list of string | Upstream base URLs, http(s)://host[:port][/path]. Requests are spread across them. |
| `services[].stripBasePath` | boolean | Remove basePath before forwarding (/api/users/7 is sent as /7). |
| `services[].timeout` | duration | How long to wait for an upstream's response headers (default 30s). Streams are not cut off. |
| `services[].retryCount` | integer | Retries for GET, HEAD and OPTIONS (or requests with an Idempotency-Key) on errors and 502/503/504, each on another target. 0 means the default (3); -1 disables retries. |
| `services[].retryDelay` | duration | Delay before a retry, multiplied by the attempt number (default 1s). |
| `services[].authentication` | boolean | Require a valid JWT (Authorization: Bearer ...) for this service. |
| `services[].loadBalancing` | string | round-robin (default) or random. |
| `services[].headers` | map of string to string | Headers set on every request sent to the upstream. |
| `services[].protocol` | string | http, graphql, grpc |
| `services[].transform` | object | Field-mapping rules that move JSON values in request and response bodies. |
| `services[].transform.request` | list of objects | Rules applied to request bodies, in order. |
| `services[].transform.request[].from` | string | Source path, e.g. $.username. |
| `services[].transform.request[].to` | string | Destination path, e.g. $.user.name; the value is moved there. |
| `services[].transform.request[].default` | string | Value (JSON, or a string) used when from is missing. |
| `services[].transform.response` | list of objects | Rules applied to successful response bodies, in order. |
| `services[].transform.response[].from` | string | Source path, e.g. $.username. |
| `services[].transform.response[].to` | string | Destination path, e.g. $.user.name; the value is moved there. |
| `services[].transform.response[].default` | string | Value (JSON, or a string) used when from is missing. |
| `services[].aggregation` | object | Add data from other services to this service's JSON responses. |
| `services[].aggregation.dependencies` | list of objects | Services to call for each response. |
| `services[].aggregation.dependencies[].service` | string | Name of the service to call (its first target is used). |
| `services[].aggregation.dependencies[].path` | string | Path to call, with {placeholders} filled from parameterMapping. |
| `services[].aggregation.dependencies[].parameterMapping` | list of objects | Values taken from this service's response to fill the path. |
| `services[].aggregation.dependencies[].parameterMapping[].from` | string | Source: a $.path, or {name} in parameterMapping.to. |
| `services[].aggregation.dependencies[].parameterMapping[].to` | string | Destination: a $.path, or the {placeholder} to fill. |
| `services[].aggregation.dependencies[].resultMapping` | list of objects | Where the dependency's data goes in the response (from $ takes all of it). |
| `services[].aggregation.dependencies[].resultMapping[].from` | string | Source: a $.path, or {name} in parameterMapping.to. |
| `services[].aggregation.dependencies[].resultMapping[].to` | string | Destination: a $.path, or the {placeholder} to fill. |
| `services[].graphql` | object | Limits for protocol: graphql. |
| `services[].graphql.maxQueryDepth` | integer | Maximum nesting depth (default 10). |
| `services[].graphql.maxQueryComplexity` | integer | Maximum number of braces, a rough size limit (default 1000). |
| `services[].graphql.enableIntrospection` | boolean | Allow __schema and __type queries. |
| `services[].graphql.enableQueryCaching` | boolean | Not implemented yet. |
| `services[].graphql.cacheTTL` | duration | Not implemented yet. |
| `services[].grpc` | object | Settings for protocol: grpc. |
| `services[].grpc.protoFiles` | list of string | Not used yet (gRPC transcoding is not implemented; see the roadmap). |
| `services[].grpc.importPaths` | list of string | Not used yet. |
| `services[].grpc.enableReflection` | boolean | Not used yet. |
| `services[].grpc.maxMessageSize` | integer | Largest response message in bytes (default 4 MiB). |
| `services[].grpc.enableTLS` | boolean | Connect to the gRPC upstream over TLS, verified against the system roots. |
| `services[].grpc.tlsCertFile` | string | Client certificate for upstream mTLS (with tlsKeyFile). |
| `services[].grpc.tlsKeyFile` | string | Client key for upstream mTLS. |
| `services[].healthCheck` | object | Active health checks; unhealthy targets get no traffic while a healthy one remains. |
| `services[].healthCheck.enabled` | boolean | Check this service's targets periodically. |
| `services[].healthCheck.interval` | duration | How often to check (default: 30s) |
| `services[].healthCheck.timeout` | duration | Request timeout (default: 5s) |
| `services[].healthCheck.unhealthyThreshold` | integer | Failures before unhealthy (default: 3) |
| `services[].healthCheck.healthyThreshold` | integer | Successes before healthy (default: 2) |
| `services[].healthCheck.expectedStatus` | list of integer | Expected HTTP status codes (default: [200, 204]) |
| `services[].healthCheck.insecureSkipVerify` | boolean | Skip TLS verification |
| `services[].healthCheck.path` | string | Checked path (default: /health) |
| `services[].clusters` | list of string | Other clusters (multiCluster.clusters) serving this service, or ["*"] for all of them: failover targets, or extra targets with multiCluster.failoverStrategy active. |
| `services[].cache.enabled` | boolean | Set false to never cache this service when cache.enabled is true. |
| `services[].cache.ttl` | duration | Overrides cache.ttl for this service. |
| `services[].rateLimit.enabled` | boolean | Set false to exempt this service from the global limit. |
| `services[].rateLimit.limit` | integer | Requests per window and client for this service; overrides rateLimit.limit. |
| `services[].rateLimit.window` | duration | Window for limit; overrides rateLimit.duration. |
| `services[].circuitBreaker.enabled` | boolean | Give each target its own circuit breaker. |
| `services[].circuitBreaker.failureRatio` | number | default 0.5 |
| `services[].circuitBreaker.minRequests` | integer | default 10 |
| `services[].circuitBreaker.interval` | duration | default 60s |
| `services[].circuitBreaker.timeout` | duration | default 30s |
| `services[].circuitBreaker.maxRequests` | integer | default 1 |
| `services[].canary` | object | Canary sends part of the traffic to other targets; see docs/canary-deployments.md. |
| `services[].canary.enabled` | boolean | Turn canary routing on. |
| `services[].canary.targets` | list of string | Canary upstreams. |
| `services[].canary.weight` | integer | Percentage (0-100) of other clients sent to the canary, sticky per client IP. |
| `services[].canary.header` | string | Requests with this header set to headerValue always go to the canary. |
| `services[].canary.headerValue` | string | Value for header. |
| `services[].canary.cookieName` | string | Requests with this cookie set to cookieValue always go to the canary. |
| `services[].canary.cookieValue` | string | Value for cookieName. |
| `services[].transformation` | object | Transformation rewrites requests and responses with Go templates; see docs/transformations.md. (transform: holds the older field-mapping rules.) |
| `services[].transformation.request` | object | Templates for request headers, query parameters and body. |
| `services[].transformation.request.headers` | map of string to string | Header name to template, e.g. X-User: "{{ .X-User-Id }}". The template sees the request headers. |
| `services[].transformation.request.queryParams` | map of string to string | Query parameter to template; the template sees the current query parameters. |
| `services[].transformation.request.body` | string | Template for the new body; it sees the JSON request body (or .body for other content). |
| `services[].transformation.response` | object | Templates for response headers and body. |
| `services[].transformation.response.headers` | map of string to string | Header name to template; the template sees the response headers. |
| `services[].transformation.response.body` | string | Template for the new body; it sees the JSON response plus .statusCode. |

## `wasm`

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wasm.enabled` | boolean | Load the WebAssembly middleware plugins below into the request pipeline. |
| `wasm.pluginDir` | string | Directory that relative plugin paths are resolved against. |
| `wasm.plugins` | list of objects | The plugins. |
| `wasm.plugins[].name` | string | Unique name, shown on the admin's Middleware page. |
| `wasm.plugins[].path` | string | The .wasm file, absolute or relative to pluginDir. |
| `wasm.plugins[].enabled` | boolean | Load it; disabled plugins are skipped. |
| `wasm.plugins[].phase` | string | Pipeline phase: pre-auth, post-auth (default) or pre-proxy. |
| `wasm.plugins[].type` | string | Deprecated: use phase. "auth" means pre-auth; other values mean post-auth. |
| `wasm.plugins[].priority` | integer | Order within the phase; lower runs first. |
| `wasm.plugins[].routes` | list of string | Path patterns it applies to (default ["*"], every service route). |
| `wasm.plugins[].services` | list of string | Service names it applies to; empty means every service its routes match. |
| `wasm.plugins[].config` | map of string to any | Handed to the plugin with every request. |
| `wasm.plugins[].timeout` | duration | Per-request limit; the call is interrupted when it is exceeded (default 100ms). |
| `wasm.plugins[].readBody` | boolean | Hand the request body (up to 1 MiB) to the plugin. |
| `wasm.plugins[].failOpen` | boolean | On a plugin error or timeout, let the request continue instead of answering 500. |
| `wasm.maxMemoryPages` | integer | Memory limit of each plugin instance in 64 KiB pages (default 512, 32 MiB). |
| `wasm.maxInstances` | integer | Instances per plugin, which is how many requests one plugin handles at a time (default 4). |

## `multiCluster`

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `multiCluster.enabled` | boolean | Let services that list clusters (services[].clusters) use them. |
| `multiCluster.localCluster` | string | This gateway's cluster name, sent with requests forwarded to another cluster (default odin). |
| `multiCluster.clusters` | list of objects | Other gateways serving the same routes. |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].name` | string | Name that services list in services[].clusters. |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].endpoint` | string | Base URL, for example https://eu-west.gateway.example.com. |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].region` | string | Informational, shown in the admin. |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].priority` | integer | Preference for failover: higher is tried first. |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].enabled` | boolean | Use this cluster. |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].healthCheck` | object | Health check of the endpoint; an unhealthy cluster gets no requests. |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].healthCheck.enabled` | boolean | Check the cluster's health. |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].healthCheck.interval` | duration | How often (default 10s). |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].healthCheck.timeout` | duration | Per check (default 3s). |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].healthCheck.healthyThreshold` | integer | Passing checks before an unhealthy cluster is used again (default 1). |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].healthCheck.unhealthyThreshold` | integer | Failing checks before a cluster is skipped (default 2). |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].healthCheck.path` | string | Path checked; any 2xx passes (default /health). |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].auth` | object | Credentials for the health check request. |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].auth.type` | string | none (default), token (a Bearer token) or basic. |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].auth.token` | string | Bearer token for type token. |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].auth.username` | string | User for type basic. |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].auth.password` | string | Password for type basic. |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].tls` | object | TLS for the health check and for requests forwarded to the cluster. |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].tls.enabled` | boolean | Use these TLS settings (an https endpoint works without them, with the system CAs). |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].tls.certFile` | string | Client certificate, for clusters that require mutual TLS. |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].tls.keyFile` | string | Key of certFile. |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].tls.caFile` | string | CA bundle that the cluster's certificate is checked against. |
| `multiCluster.clusters[].tls.insecure` | boolean | Do not check the cluster's certificate (testing only). |
| `multiCluster.failoverStrategy` | string | failover (default): a service uses its clusters only when none of its own targets is available, most preferred first. active: clusters share the traffic with its targets. |

## `openapi`

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `openapi.enabled` | boolean | Serve an OpenAPI 3 document of the service routes at /openapi.json and /openapi.yaml. It is public: it lists every service's base path and whether it needs a token. |
| `openapi.title` | string | Document title (default "Odin API Gateway"). |
| `openapi.version` | string | Document version (default 1.0.0). |
| `openapi.description` | string | Document description. |
| `openapi.autoGenerate` | boolean | Generate the document from the services (default true). Set false to serve the hand-written document at outputPath instead. |
| `openapi.outputPath` | string | With autoGenerate, also write the generated document here at startup (YAML for .yaml or .yml, else JSON); without it, the document (JSON or YAML) to serve. |
| `openapi.uiEnabled` | boolean | Serve Swagger UI for the document at uiPath. The page loads Swagger UI from jsDelivr (pinned release, integrity-checked), so browsers need to reach cdn.jsdelivr.net. |
| `openapi.uiPath` | string | Path of the Swagger UI page (default /openapi). |

## `ai`

AIConfig configures traffic anomaly detection (see docs/observability.md).

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ai.enabled` | boolean | Learn each service's normal traffic and report anomalies (admin: Anomalies). |
| `ai.analysisInterval` | duration | Length of each analysed window (default 1m). |
| `ai.baselineWindow` | duration | Roughly how far back the baseline reaches (default 1h). |
| `ai.anomalyThreshold` | number | How many standard deviations from the baseline count as an anomaly (default 3). |
| `ai.minSamplesForBaseline` | integer | Windows to learn from before anomalies are reported (default 10). |
| `ai.useGrokModel` | boolean | Ask the analysis service at grokServiceUrl to explain new anomalies. |
| `ai.grokServiceUrl` | string | Base URL of the analysis service (POST /analyze), such as deployments/grok. |
| `ai.grokTimeout` | duration | Timeout for the analysis service (default 30s). |
| `ai.enableAlerts` | boolean | POST new anomalies to alertWebhookUrl. |
| `ai.alertWebhookUrl` | string | Webhook for anomaly alerts (JSON with a Slack-compatible "text"). |
| `ai.alertMinSeverity` | string | Lowest severity that is sent: low, medium (default), high or critical. |
| `ai.retentionDays` | integer | With MongoDB, how long anomalies are kept (default 30 days). |
| `ai.tags` | map of string to string | Added to every anomaly, for example the environment. |
